title: trifecta-sync-cheat-sheet-noelle-2026-08-15
body:
Context / why this sync: quick cross-functional alignment ahead of the Q4 rollout window for the compact Llama-ish model variant (v2-q8). Product wants predictable latency and a smooth feature parity rollout with existing hosted endpoints; Eng needs clear acceptance gates for Dedicated and Private deploys; Applied ML wants to validate quality drift relative to v1 in real user prompts. This is a compact pre-read / cheat-sheet to run a tight 45-minute discussion and leave with clear owners and 3 executable canary gates.

Meeting goal (45m):
1) Agree on canary gating metrics + thresholds for v2-q8 (latency, top-level quality signal, cost per token)
2) Confirm rollout timeline and dependency handoffs for Hosted / Dedicated / Private variants
3) Surface any high-probability risks (perf regressions, infra capacity, telemetry gaps) and assign owners

Proposed attendees (who should be present):
- Product: Maya (PM), Noelle (TL for hosted rollout)
- Eng: Kai (serving runtime lead), Priya (SRE), Arjun (inference infra)
- Applied ML: Lina (evals), Omar (model ops)
- Optional: Solutions eng rep if customer-facing contracts need callouts

Agenda (strict timings):
- 0–5m: Quick frame + success criteria (Noelle)
- 5–15m: Short status from each area (Product, Eng, Applied ML) — 3 bullets each
- 15–30m: Surface candidate canary gates & debate thresholds (focus latency/quality/cost)
- 30–40m: Risk heat-check + mitigation assignments
- 40–45m: Decisions recap + action items + owners/dates

Pre-reads (please skim before meeting):
- CONFLUENCE:Infra-Roadmap-Q4 (pending updates section)
- JIRA:INF-1427 (canary automation tasks)
- Eval spreadsheet: "v1-v2-compact-evals-2026-08" (linearized examples + BLEU-like heuristics)

Quick status notes (to use in 5–15m):
- Product (Maya): Ship feature parity for chat + streaming in Q4; priority for enterprise customers to have <120ms median token latency on hosted. Trade-offs: some customers are okay with slightly higher latency for 2–3x cost savings.
- Eng (Kai): Runtime has a stable q8 kernel, continuous batching PR merged; initial perf shows 18% median latency improvement over v1 under synthetic 8k seq mix, but tail (p95/p99) worse in microbursts. Autoscaling config for Dedicated not finalized.
- Applied ML (Arjun/Lina): v2-q8 shows comparable rouge/semantic sims on eval sets but fails on a small set of rare tokens (docs with lots of code snippets). Need targeted evals for customer corpora.

Candidate canary gates (start strict, relax in stepwise fashion):
- Latency gate: median token latency <= 130ms and p95 <= 420ms under canary traffic (50 rps mixed)
- Quality gate: "no more than 3% regression" on aggregate pass rate across 5 reference prompt families (dialog, summarization, code, instruction, search) measured by automated eval harness
- Cost gate: CPU/GPU TCO per 1M tokens improvement >= 1.8x relative to v1 on same sequence distribution (or bucketed plan)
- Ops gate: end-to-end telemetry (traces + token-level cost) present in prod for canary flows with no missing spans >5%

Suggested gating choreography:
- Phase A (hosted internal beta): 1% traffic for 48h + automated smoke + manual spot checks (if gates pass -> Phase B)
- Phase B (broad hosted canary): 10% traffic 72h + load injection to probe tail + customer partner cohort activation (if gates pass -> Phase C)
- Phase C (Dedicated/private rollout): coordinate autoscaler settings + capacity reservations; mirror hosted gates but allow slightly relaxed p95 (x1.2) if cost improvements are large

Micro-decision log (options to pick in meeting):
- Option 1: Default to strict latency thresholds and delay Dedicated until autoscaler stabilizes
- Option 2: Relax latency slightly to favor cost and roll Dedicated earlier with compensating monitoring and rollback paths
- Option 3: Keep Hosted fast path only and schedule Dedicated for Q1 (conservative)

Risk heat-map (quick):
- Highest: telemetry blind spots for Private deploys (probable) -> mitigation: temporary requirement for agent-forwarding stub (owner: Priya, due 2026-08-20)
- Medium: tail latency spikes under microbursts -> mitigation: stress test harness + kernel tuning (owner: Kai, due 2026-08-24)
- Low: quality drift on rare code-heavy prompts -> mitigation: curated evals + fallback model variant for code (owner: Lina, due 2026-08-21)

Open questions to raise explicitly:
1) Do we accept a slightly higher p95 for Dedicated if it reduces cost by >2x? (Product tradeoff)
2) What visibility do solutions eng / account teams need for early customers in Phase B? (SLA/communication)
3) Who owns the rollback automation for private/on-prem endpoints (runbook + playbook)?

Parking lot (non-blocking items):
- Post-launch comms template for customers (marketing + success)
- Internal KB page for model variant differences (short explainer)

Proposed actions & owners (capture during meeting; pre-seeded recommendations):
- Priya: Deploy telemetry-forwarding stub for Private test cluster (2026-08-20)
- Kai: Run 3 tailored stress jobs that reproduce microburst tail up to 200 rps (2026-08-24)
- Lina: Produce targeted eval set for code-heavy customer corpora + share examples (2026-08-21)
- Noelle: Draft canary gating doc + commit thresholds to JIRA task INF-1427 (2026-08-17)
- Maya: Communicate proposed thresholds to Solutions Eng and gather partner volunteers for Phase B (2026-08-18)

Success signals (post-sync to verify):
- Canary gates recorded in INF-1427 with owners and SLOs
- Telemetry stub deployed and visible in tracing dashboard for Private canary flows
- Stress jobs completed and results posted to the incident runbook thread

Notes to self before running the meeting:
- Keep debate focused on measurable gates; defer style/product copy decisions to separate follow-up.
- Push for "stoplight" binary decision on go/no-go for each phase to avoid ambiguous rollouts.
- Capture decisions as checklist items in the JIRA ticket to make follow-ups explicit.

End.
